messages:
maria: heads up — hitting a sustained drop in prefix-cache hit rate for the /summarize route on model `redwood/gpt-4-xl-compat` starting after the kernel selector change yesterday. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.dev/rl/2345 :eyes:

metrics-bot: ALERT: prefix_cache.hit_rate decrease (route=/summarize, model=gpt-4-xl-compat) 10m avg 0.41 -> 0.28 (tokens_saved delta -22%) — investigate

tony: ugh. saw a small perf regression locally when the selector moved to the new fused-attn kernel. wondered if batching behavior changed too. are we seeing fewer prefix-reuse events per batch?

ash: quick look at the slice: per-tenant heatmap shows the biggest delta on tenant:acme_prod and route=/summarize/long. key churn is up. my hunch: kernel change altered tokenization alignment for a tiny fraction of inputs causing different prefix fingerprints.

maria: snippet of the query I ran for the dashboard (per-route, per-model, per-tenant):
```
SELECT route, tenant, model, avg(hit_rate) as hit_rate, sum(tokens_saved) as tokens_saved
FROM prefix_cache_metrics
WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '6h'
GROUP BY route, tenant, model
ORDER BY tokens_saved desc
```

tony: can we confirm whether batching heuristics also changed? the new kernel has lower per-token latency which might reduce folding windows and increase smaller batches -> more KV keys generated per second.

ash: good point. quick sample from profiler: 
```
kv_write_rate(route=/summarize) : 1200/s -> 1850/s
avg_batch_size(model=gpt-4-xl-compat) : 6.8 -> 4.1
key_entropy(route=/summarize) : 0.62 -> 0.78
```

ops-sre: ops note — we already have a canary pinned to the previous kernel on a small pool. we can route 5% of acme_prod traffic back to pinned pool to measure rollback impact on hit-rate and tokens_saved. want to avoid broad rollback if warmup seeding fixes it.

maria: proposed mitigation plan: 1) run 5% rollback to pinned kernel for acme_prod /summarize for 6 hours; 2) add a targeted warmup job that injects 50k high-frequency prefixes (seed corpus from last 7 days) for that route + model on the new kernel; 3) add dashboard panels: per-model delta tokens_saved, key_entropy, avg_batch_size, warmup_coverage.

tony: +1. also try toggling `max_batch_delay_ms` from 12 -> 20 on the new kernel pool to see if slightly larger folding restores avg_batch_size and hit-rate. low-risk A/B.

ash: i'll run the warmup seeds script and capture before/after metrics. warmup script: 
```bash
./tools/warmup_prefetch --tenant acme_prod --route /summarize --model redwood/gpt-4-xl-compat --count 50000 --concurrency 16
```

ops-sre: i'll spin the 5% rollback canary and a pipeline to snapshot the dashboard every 10m. please post links to the snapshot panels.

maria: metrics to watch (agreed): `[prefix_cache.hit_rate]`, `[tokens_saved]`, `[avg_batch_size]`, `[kv_write_rate]`, `[key_entropy]`, `[cold_warmup_coverage]`. if tokens_saved recovers and key_entropy falls back we can proceed without full rollback.

tony: timeline: start canary + warmup in 15m, collect 6h, decision call at +6h. i'm owner for the `max_batch_delay` A/B.

ash: assigned: warmup + metric snapshots. will update thread with first snapshot link in ~20m. :thumbsup:

metrics-bot: SNAPSHOT: dashboard snapshot created: https://dash.redwood.dev/snapshots/3a9f2b (contains per-tenant token savings and key_entropy panels)

maria: perfect. thanks all — let's keep comms here. if we see degradation widen to other tenants we escalate.

tony: noted.
